'alcohol thermometer' is rendered with the established compound 'vínandahitamælis'; applying alkóhól would require coining a new compound.

'temperature change' is rendered hitabreytingu; temperature is ruled hitastig, but it is the first part of the established compound, so applying it would need a new compound.

'Specific heat capacity' is rendered Eðlisvarmarýmd; the ruled eðlisvarmi is masculine, so the pronoun Hún at the start of the next sentence would also need to become Hann.
'the molten salt mixture' is rendered saltblandan; applying efnablanda would need a new compound (saltefnablandan), so it was left unchanged.

'Heat transfer fluid' is rendered Varmaskiptivökvi; heat transfer is ruled varmaflutningur, which here would be the first part of the compound, not its head. Another segment of this module uses varmaflutningsvökvi, so an editor may want Varmaflutningsvökvi.
'melting temperature' is rendered with the established word bræðslumark; applying temperature → hitastig would need a new compound, so it was left unchanged.

'reaction mixture' is rendered with the established compound hvarfblönduna; applying mixture → efnablanda would need a new compound (hvarfefnablanda), so it was left unchanged for an editor to decide.

'liquid mixture' is Vökvablandan and 'Reaction mixture' is Hvarfblanda, both established compounds with head blanda. Putting in efnablanda would coin Vökvaefnablandan and Hvarfefnablanda; an editor should decide whether these may stand.
'temperature sensor' is rendered with the established compound hitaskynjara. Applying hitastig would coin hitastigsskynjara; an editor should decide whether it may stand.
'temperature probe' is rendered with the established compound hitanemi. Applying hitastig would coin hitastigsnemi; an editor should decide whether it may stand.
The attributive 'precision temperature probe' is rendered with the adjective Nákvæmur. The ruled noun nákvæmni cannot replace it without rebuilding the phrase (e.g. hitanemi með mikilli nákvæmni).

'had been submerged in boiling water' is rendered 'hafði verið sökkt í sjóðandi vatn'. The ruled target is 'á kafi', which would also need the noun changed to dative ('á kafi í sjóðandi vatni'). That cannot be done with a term change alone.

'was submerged in boiling water' is rendered 'var sökkt í sjóðandi vatn', which is also ungrammatical with the subject 'málmurinn'. The ruled target 'á kafi' would need 'málmurinn var á kafi í sjóðandi vatni', which changes the case of the noun.
'two significant figures' is rendered 'tvær markverðar tölur'; the ruled term is markverðir stafir (masculine), which would need the number word tvær changed to tveir, so it was not edited.

'no heat is absorbed' is 'enginn hiti' and 'no heat is exchanged' is 'engin hitaskipti'; heat is ruled varmi, but the quantifier enginn/engin stands next to the term, so it was not edited (consider 'enginn varmi' and 'engin varmaskipti').
'Heat Flow' is rendered Hitastreymi, where heat is the first part, not the head; applying varmi would mean changing the compound's modifier (e.g. Varmastreymi), which an editor should decide.

'The temperature change' is rendered Hitabreytingin, with hiti as the first part; temperature is ruled hitastig, which would need a different compound (e.g. Hitastigsbreytingin, cf. Hitastigshækkunin earlier).

'Calories per day' and 'one Calorie' (capital C, the nutritional calorie of 1 kcal) are rendered hitaeiningum and ein hitaeining. The calorie target kaloría would erase the Calorie/calorie distinction, and 'ein' blocks an edit. An editor should decide whether næringarkaloría is meant.
'One calorie (cal)' is Ein kalóría. The ruled spelling is kaloría, but the number word Ein blocks an automatic edit.

'Calories' and 'one Calorie (note the capitalization)' mean the nutritional calorie (1 kcal) and are rendered hitaeiningum and ein hitaeining. Using kaloría here would be wrong. An editor should decide whether næringarkaloría is meant, and the capitalization note may need rewording.

'the measured temperature change' is rendered hitabreyting. The first part hita- renders temperature (ruled hitastig), and only a head may be swapped, so an editor should decide whether to use hitastigsbreyting.

'room temperature' is the established compound stofuhita. Applying temperature → hitastig would need a new compound (stofuhitastig), so it was left for an editor; all other uses already have hitastig.
The subscript labels [[sub:varmaefnamælir]] (for q_calorimeter) still use varmaefnamælir and cannot be edited here; an editor should change them to varmamælir.
'Calorie content' is hitaeiningainnihald; calorie is ruled kaloría, but the term is the first part of the compound, not its head, so it cannot be swapped.

The three identical 'hitaeining/g' (Calories/g) and 'meðalfjöldi hitaeininga' should use kaloría, but the unit forms sit between numbers and slashes and cannot be targeted individually; an editor should change them all together with the compound.

The term label for 'chemical thermodynamics' reads varmaefnafræði, which means thermochemistry, so the sentence says thermochemistry is a branch of itself. It should be efnavarmafræði. No edit was made because the same word occurs again later in the segment and the label cannot be targeted uniquely; an editor should change the label to efnavarmafræði.

'room-temperature' is rendered with the established compound stofuhita (við stofuhita). Applying temperature → hitastig would create the compound stofuhitastig, so no edit was made; an editor should decide whether to keep stofuhita.

'The system loses energy by both heating and doing work on the surroundings' is rendered with 'með því að hitna' (by becoming hot), not by heating the surroundings. This reverses the physics; an editor should check this clause.

'extensive property' is rendered útþenslueiginleika/útþenslueiginleikanum; ruled magnbundinn eiginleiki, but the first use stands next to the number word einum (and öðrum), so the ruling was not applied anywhere in this segment.

'molar heats of formation' is rendered with the single compound mólmyndunarhitum; swapping the head to varmi (mólmyndunarvörmum) would create a new compound, so an editor should choose the established term for heat of formation.

'high temperature and pressure' is 'háan hita og þrýsting'; temperature is ruled hitastig, which is neuter and would need 'háan' changed to 'hátt' (not a simple ending change), and the shared adjective with 'þrýsting' needs a look.
